analysis.title: First Read: NVIDIA Corp - Board of Directors Reinstates Jensen; Our Thoughts
key_insights: NVDA announced Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO on 23 Nov 2026. UBS calls it a clear positive and says it is consistent with its decision to keep the Buy rating rather than downgrade.
His departure had created uncertainty around financing, supply-chain strategy and talent retention. UBS expects these concerns to recede.
The land powered shell issue is not going away, especially if President Trump follows through on Friday comments dissuading companies from building data centers outside the US.
UBS expects NVDA management structure could become more hierarchical to enable clearer succession plans.
NVDA could pull back on ecosystem financing, but it has about $390B of supply commitments. UBS says it likely needs to keep the flywheel running to stimulate demand offtake.
US intelligence linking Megaspeed to Chinese intelligence could drive more hawkish export controls, such as new Commerce Entity List additions or passage of the MATCH Act.
UBS warns MATCH would have broader negative implications across tech hardware through 'matched set' issues similar to the COVID period.
Focus for NVDA should shift back to execution, the product roadmap and the broader AI opportunity.
Rating Buy and PT $220 unchanged, based on about 12x C2028E P/E on C2028E EPS of $18.80. The stock was $169.27 on 23 Nov 2026, implying 30.0% forecast price appreciation.
PT history shows cuts from $300 (27 Aug 2026) to $240 (16 Nov) and $220 (18 Nov) as the stock fell from $227.98 to $150.96.
UBS EPS estimates are above consensus for 01/28E ($17.82 vs $16.78) and below for 01/29E ($18.80 vs $21.78). FY 01/27E is $9.71 vs $9.65.

market_movers.rationale: Jensen Huang's CEO reinstatement removes financing, supply-chain and talent uncertainty. PT unchanged at about 12x C2028E EPS of $18.80.

sector_views.rationale: Buy on NVDA, with focus returning to execution and AI opportunity. Export control and MATCH Act risks flagged for tech hardware.

earnings_insights: UBS EPS (diluted) estimate FY 01/27E $9.71 vs consensus $9.65, FY 01/28E $17.82 vs consensus $16.78, FY 01/29E $18.80 vs consensus $21.78. All are estimates.
UBS FY 01/27E revenue estimate $427,223m and FY 01/28E $770,708m. Reported FY 01/26 revenue was $215,938m.
UBS Q4E FY01/27 EPS estimate $2.94 vs consensus $2.88. Reported Q1 to Q3 were $1.87, $2.22 and $2.68.
UBS Quant Review gives no view on next EPS surprise and shows no catalyst over the next three months.
risk_factors: Export controls, Entity List additions and the MATCH Act could hit NVDA and broader tech hardware.
Restrictions on building data centers outside the US, with land powered shell issue persisting.
Possible pullback in ecosystem financing against about $390B of supply commitments.
Management structure changes and succession uncertainty.
Competition from AMD and Intel, and semiconductor cyclicality.
geopolitical: US intelligence established connections at Megaspeed to Chinese intelligence, which could drive more hawkish export control actions.
Possible new additions to the US Department of Commerce Entity List or passage of the MATCH Act.
President Trump's Friday comments dissuading companies from building data centers outside the US.

tension_points.bull_case: Huang's return removes uncertainty on financing, supply chain and talent, so focus returns to execution and roadmap.
tension_points.bear_case: Land powered shell restrictions and tougher export controls such as MATCH could weigh on NVDA and tech hardware.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Passage of the MATCH Act or new Entity List additions would challenge the positive read.
